security_audit.summary: All 226 static findings are false positives caused by documentation examples, Markdown backticks, deployment configuration, and benign scoped checks. No prompt injection, secret exfiltration, or malicious automation was found. The skill does recommend executing unpinned latest-tag packages, which creates a medium supply-chain risk.

remediation.suggestion: Prefer a reviewed, pinned package version or require users to inspect the resolved package before executing it.

remediation.issue: The agent installer delegates to skills@latest through a package runner.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation and pin or verify the installer source before installing or updating skills.

remediation.issue: Deployment examples can load environment files.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before commands that upload environment values and remind users to use only intended secret files.

content.value_statement: Prisma Compute deployments require correct configuration, authentication, environment settings, and runtime ports. This skill guides setup, deployment, verification, and troubleshooting for supported TypeScript frameworks.
actual_capabilities: Explains Prisma Compute CLI deployment workflows for existing applications.
Guides creation and review of prisma.compute.ts configuration files.
Checks framework build output, host binding, and HTTP port requirements.
Explains workspace selection, project targeting, and branch deployment scope.
Distinguishes build logs from runtime logs during troubleshooting.
Describes SDK and Management API paths for lower-level automation.
limitations: It cannot deploy, promote, remove, or modify an application without tool access and user approval.
It does not validate live Prisma account permissions or platform service status.
It cannot recover secrets or create a valid database connection string.
CLI behavior can change, so command help should be checked before execution.

use_cases.title: Prepare an existing service
use_cases.description: Review an existing TypeScript service for Compute configuration, build output, environment inputs, and port binding.

use_cases.title: Deploy a preview branch
use_cases.description: Plan a branch deployment with explicit project, app, branch, and preview environment settings.

use_cases.title: Resolve deployment failures
use_cases.description: Separate authentication, build, database, and runtime failures using the correct CLI output and logs.

prompt_templates.title: Review deployment readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my project for Prisma Compute deployment readiness. Check the framework, build command, port binding, and required configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Create Compute configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a prisma.compute.ts configuration for my application. Ask for the app root, framework, entrypoint, HTTP port, and environment file path.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a preview deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a safe Prisma Compute preview deployment for my branch. Identify the explicit project, app, branch, and environment settings before proposing commands.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot a failed deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose my Prisma Compute deployment failure. First classify it as authentication, build, environment, database, or runtime, then list the least invasive checks.

output_examples.input: Review my Next.js app before deployment.
output: Framework: Next.js with standalone server output required.
Runtime: bind to the deployment port and all interfaces.
Next step: verify the generated deployment script and configuration.

output_examples.input: My preview deployment cannot connect to the database.
output: Check that the branch name matches the branch environment scope.
Confirm a non-placeholder database URL is available to the deployment.
Use runtime logs after verifying environment configuration.
Inspect the active workspace before changing project or app state.
Select an explicit workspace identifier for non-interactive work.
Do not display service tokens or local credential files.

best_practices: Check CLI help and the existing project configuration before running deployment commands.
Use explicit workspace, project, app, and branch identifiers for automated operations.
Keep secrets in platform or CI storage and never print connection URLs or tokens.
anti_patterns: Do not deploy to production without clear user intent and a review of the target.
Do not use placeholder database URLs or commit secret values to configuration files.
Do not treat local readiness as proof that the public deployment is reachable.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy an application automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and should request confirmation before commands that change remote applications.

faq.question: Which frameworks does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers documented Compute readiness guidance for Next.js, Nuxt, Astro, Hono, NestJS, TanStack Start, custom apps, and Bun.

faq.question: Should I commit prisma.compute.ts?
faq.answer: You can commit non-secret deployment defaults. Keep tokens, connection strings, and secret values outside version control.

faq.question: How should I handle several workspaces?
faq.answer: Inspect local sessions and select an explicit workspace identifier before non-interactive changes.

faq.question: Does deployment run database migrations?
faq.answer: No. Run migrations and seed tasks separately through the appropriate database workflow.

faq.question: What logs should I inspect after a failure?
faq.answer: Use build logs for build failures and application logs for runtime deployment failures.
